summary: BCP 172 (RFC 6472) advised against using AS_SET and AS_CONFED_SET path segments in BGP. This RFC turns that advice into a requirement for BGP: those segment types are prohibited in the AS_PATH. The change simplifies BGP design and operation. It obsoletes RFC 6472.

eli5.summary: Route announcements used to allow a messy "unordered pile" of network names. This says to stop using that pile, which makes the route lists simpler.

questions: what is brief aggregation in bgp
subtitle: BGP routers may no longer announce routes with an unordered set of ASes in the path, which makes the origin of a route clear.

tldr.problem: When a BGP router aggregates several routes, it may put an unordered AS_SET (or AS_CONFED_SET) in the AS_PATH. That blurs which AS originated the route and complicates BGP security tools such as RPKI-based Route Origin Validation.
tldr.mechanism: BGP speakers MUST NOT advertise UPDATE messages containing AS_SETs or AS_CONFED_SETs, and MUST treat-as-withdraw any received UPDATE that contains them. Operators aggregate with consistent brief aggregation instead, which keeps the origin AS predictable.
tldr.outcome: The recommendation of BCP 172 (RFC 6472) becomes a standards requirement, and RFC 6472 is obsoleted. RFC 4271 and RFC 5065 are updated.

today: RFC 9774 is a Proposed Standard, published in May 2025. It obsoletes RFC 6472 and updates RFC 4271 and RFC 5065; no later RFC is recorded as obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: From Advice to Requirement
sections.content:
BCP 172, which is RFC 6472, recommended not using the AS_SET and AS_CONFED_SET path segment types in the AS_PATH of the Border Gateway Protocol (BGP). RFC 9774 advances that recommendation to a standards requirement: the use of both segment types in the AS_PATH is prohibited.

The stated purposes are to simplify the design and implementation of BGP, to make the semantics of the originator of a route clearer, and to simplify the design, implementation and deployment of BGP security mechanisms. In particular, banning the sets removes any ambiguity about the origin AS in RPKI-based Route Origin Validation (RPKI-ROV).

The RFC updates RFC 4271 by deprecating origination of routes with AS_SET (a Type 1 AS_PATH segment) and updates RFC 5065 by deprecating origination of routes with AS_CONFED_SET (a Type 4 segment). It also obsoletes RFC 6472.
sections.eli5: The old advice said 'please do not use the messy pile of names'. Now it is a rule, not just advice.

sections.title: What AS_SET and AS_CONFED_SET Are
sections.content:
An AS_SET is created by a router that is performing route aggregation. It holds an unordered set of Autonomous Systems (ASes) that the contributing prefixes in the aggregate have traversed. An AS_CONFED_SET is very similar, but it is created inside a confederation and holds the Member AS Numbers that the contributing prefixes have traversed.

Aggregation combines several routes for more specific destinations into one route for a less specific destination. Doing so can blur the origin AS of the announced prefix. Because the origin cannot be authenticated, new BGP security technologies that use X.509 extensions for IP addresses and AS identifiers can have trouble with such routes, which could cause reachability problems for the destinations in the aggregate.

The authors also cite an analysis of historical Internet routing data. It shows aggregation involving AS_SETs is very seldom used on the public Internet, and when it is used it is often used incorrectly. A single AS in the set is the most common case, the same AS often appears in both the AS_SEQUENCE and the AS_SET, and reserved AS numbers show up fairly often.
sections.eli5: When a router bundles many routes into one, it used to be allowed to attach a jumbled list of every network involved. That list made it hard to say who the bundle really came from.

sections.title: The New Rules for BGP Speakers
sections.content:
Unless a network operator explicitly configures otherwise (for example during a transition phase), BGP speakers:

  • MUST NOT advertise BGP UPDATE messages containing AS_SETs or AS_CONFED_SETs, and
  • MUST use the treat-as-withdraw error handling behavior from RFC 7606 when they receive an UPDATE message containing AS_SETs or AS_CONFED_SETs in the AS_PATH or AS4_PATH (the latter defined in RFC 6793).

Treat-as-withdraw means the affected routes are handled as if they had been withdrawn. This is how the RFC deprecates AS_SET (RFC 4271, Section 4.3) and AS_CONFED_SET (RFC 5065, Section 3).
sections.eli5: Routers must not send the jumbled list anymore. If one arrives anyway, the router acts as if that route was taken back.

sections.title: Effect on RPKI-Based BGP Security
sections.content:
The Resource Public Key Infrastructure (RPKI) uses X.509 extensions for IP addresses and AS identifiers. Several BGP security technologies build on it, and none of them handles AS_SET well:

  • RPKI-ROV never allows a route with an AS_SET to be considered Valid.
  • BGPsec does not support AS_SETs.
  • In ASPA-based AS_PATH verification, a route with an AS_SET is always considered Invalid and so is ineligible for route selection.

Removing AS_SETs from BGP therefore lets these tools work on every route.
sections.eli5: The tools that check who a route really comes from either reject or cannot read the jumbled list. Without it, they can do their job.

sections.title: Brief Aggregation and Consistent Brief Aggregation
sections.content:
When AS_PATH aggregation follows RFC 4271, Section 9.2.2.2 and any resulting AS_SETs are discarded, implementations call it brief aggregation. The aggregate keeps the longest leading sequence of path tuples common to all the contributing routes, and the ATOMIC_AGGREGATE attribute is attached if AS_SETs are dropped.

Brief aggregation has no AS_SET, but the origin AS of the result can still be unpredictable. It can vary with which contributing routes happen to be present, and the resource holder would need to register a ROA for each potential origin AS.

To fix this, an implementation of brief aggregation MUST be configured to truncate the AS_PATH after the right-most instance of the desired origin AS for the aggregate. The desired origin could be the aggregating AS itself, and a ROA is needed for the aggregate prefix with that origin AS. This is called consistent brief aggregation. If the path is truncated compared with the otherwise expected result, ATOMIC_AGGREGATE SHOULD be attached.
sections.eli5: Instead of a jumbled list, the router cuts the list at one clear starting network and says so. Everyone then knows where the bundle claims to come from.

sections.title: Operational Advice
sections.content:
When aggregating prefixes, network operators MUST use consistent brief aggregation. The AGGREGATOR and ATOMIC_AGGREGATE attributes are included, but the AS_PATH has no AS_SET or AS_CONFED_SET segments.

An aggregate prefix SHOULD NOT be announced to the contributing ASes. Instead, the more specific prefixes SHOULD be announced to each contributing AS, leaving out any that were learned from that same AS.

Without AS_SETs, a contributing AS no longer rejects the aggregate through AS_PATH loop detection, so forwarding loops become possible. The RFC points to Rule #2 in Section 5.1 of RFC 4632: a router that generates an aggregate must discard packets that match the aggregate route but none of the more specific routes, so the next hop for the aggregate is the null destination.
sections.eli5: Do not hand the bundle back to the networks that built it, and throw away mail that fits the bundle but has no real street to go to.

sections.title: Worked Examples from the Appendices
sections.content:
Appendix B uses AS 64500 aggregating four /26 routes into 192.0.2.0/24. With ordinary brief aggregation the resulting AS_PATH depends on which routes arrived: it can truncate to the empty path "" or to "64504", so it is not stable.

Consistent brief aggregation fixes this. The trivial solution is to discard all of the contributing ASes and originate the aggregate with AS 64500 itself, so one ROA covers it. If the contributing ASes are multihomed outside their connections to AS 64500, additional ROAs are needed for the more specific prefixes. Where all contributing paths share a neighbor AS, such as AS 64504, the aggregate's path may be kept as "64504", with a ROA naming 64504 as origin.

Appendix A shows AS 64505 aggregating four /24 prefixes into p/22 with an empty AS_PATH, AGGREGATOR and ATOMIC_AGGREGATE. The aggregate is not announced to the four contributing ASes, which avoids data plane loops.
sections.eli5: The examples show that, with a plain cut, the starting point can change depending on which routes showed up. Choosing the starting point on purpose keeps it steady.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: Deprecating aggregation techniques that create AS_SETs or AS_CONFED_SETs, and removing the related code from implementations, would potentially decrease the attack surface for BGP. New BGP security technologies such as RPKI (RFC 6480), RPKI-ROV (RFC 6811) and BGPsec (RFC 8205) benefit greatly when these segment types are not used. The document has no IANA actions.
sections.eli5: Fewer odd corner cases means fewer places for attackers to hide.
